topic: Shashtamsa D6 — the health varga and how to use it cautiously (DD deep-dive reel, English, 2026-09-10 pm, guard: health-disclaimer)

slides.sub: The D6 — the divisional chart traditionally read for health, and its limits

slides.body:
Astrology is not diagnosis and it is not treatment. If something is wrong, see a doctor. No chart, no varga and no dasha can identify an illness, and nobody should delay medical care because of one.

What follows is a description of a classical technique and where it is legitimately weak. Read it as method, not as medicine.

A varga (divisional chart) splits each sign into equal parts and maps each part onto a full zodiac, so a single degree of the birth chart opens into a whole second chart.

The Shashtamsa is the sixth division — each 30° sign cut into six parts of 5° each. It is abbreviated D6, and Parashara assigns it to arogya: health, resistance, and the sixth-house matters generally.

points: Take a planet's position and find which 5° part of its sign it occupies
For odd signs, the count most texts give begins from Mesha
For even signs, that count begins from Tula
The sign you land on is that planet's D6 position
Texts do vary on this rule — know which convention your software uses

slides.body:
The D6 is an amplifier, never a starting point. The order that keeps you honest:

1. The 6th house of the birth chart and its lord. 2. The rogesha (6th lord) chain and its dispositor. 3. The Lagna and Lagna lord — vitality lives there. 4. Only then the D6, to see whether it echoes what D1 already said. If D6 says something D1 does not, D1 wins.

Not every varga is equally attested. The D1, D9 and D10 carry centuries of continuous use; the D6 is thinly documented by comparison, and classical texts give it far less commentary than its reputation online suggests.

A 5° division is also unforgiving of birth-time error — a few minutes of uncertainty can move a planet a whole sign in D6. That is a real limitation, not a technicality.

Comment — most consultations never open it, and the ones that do rarely mention the birth-time sensitivity.

Saying it once more, because it matters: astrology is not diagnosis or treatment. See a doctor. Save this and follow along.
